fields.title: Long context has several axes: position, access, and state compression
fields.thesis: Ask first how history is stored and then how the current token reads it. RoPE changes relative position relationships; Mamba writes history into recurrence; NSA splits access across paths; OpenAttention retains proxies for unread content; and TTR fits an input-conditioned compression. MERLIN keeps routing-key moments beside compressed segment states to change how segments are read without replacing their internal recurrent writes. A single supported-length number cannot rank these designs.
fields.axis_0: Token-level KV, recurrent state, or input-conditioned compression coefficients
fields.axis_1: Whether the current query can revisit exact details
fields.axis_2: Whether unread history is omitted, summarized, or already folded into state
fields.axis_3: Costs in training, forward solving, or index access

fields.position: Rotate two-dimensional Q/K subspaces so their dot product expresses relative position; compatible with full attention.
fields.tradeoff: Encodes position rather than reducing history count or KV bandwidth. The local small-model rotation does not establish arbitrary length extrapolation.

fields.position: Use token-conditioned step size and read/write vectors to fold history into bounded recurrent state.
fields.tradeoff: Avoids retaining all token KV, but only information kept in state remains accessible. Local native PyTorch scan does not reproduce the fused kernel.

fields.position: Use compressed blocks for overview, query-selected blocks for detail, and a sliding window for exact recency; gate their outputs together.
fields.tradeoff: Different paths need design and training. A coarse overview may not recover details after a selection miss. Local trainability is not reported long-context throughput.

fields.position: Cluster by query geometry, allocate exact-read budget by estimated proxy error, and include unread clusters as count-weighted mean proxies in softmax.
fields.tradeoff: The tail is not zeroed, but within-cluster detail can disappear and ErrorGate relies on approximations. Only a single-head operator is diagnosed locally; full experiments were too expensive.

fields.position: Treat token groups as regression observations and solve regularized least squares each forward pass for input-conditioned coefficients.
fields.tradeoff: Neither weight training at inference nor free pooling. The dual solve has a T³ term and is attractive only when groups are much shorter than feature width. Local work is diagnostic.

fields.position: Aggregate top-k low-CE positions of query tokens, scale by T×softmax, and clip write multipliers.
fields.tradeoff: Requires a real frozen head/RMSNorm and NTP-aligned features, not a local LLM or distributed kernel.

fields.position: Mix an external binary semantic reward with thresholded token edit similarity.
fields.tradeoff: Implements LTI reward only, not CMS, dreaming, knowledge seeding, or LoRA; full Sleep training was too expensive and not reproduced.

fields.position: Keep segment routing-key means and raw second moments to recover query-aligned variance. Softmax the two paths separately and gate their external state readouts.
fields.tradeoff: Adds segment-state and moment storage without reconstructing exact token softmax. The current unfinished segment needs external recurrence; full mid-training was not reproduced.

fields.title: Expressible position is not accessible history
fields.body: RoPE defines how QK carries relative position, but full attention still processes visible history. Mamba changes storage and propagation, replacing per-token access with state. Position extrapolation failure and forgetting a detail in state are different; extra state alone cannot explain the former and changing positions cannot fix the latter. Identify whether the task needs exact lookup or persistent state updates.

fields.title: Can compressed history still expose details?
fields.body: NSA's compressed branch sits beside query-conditioned exact block reads. OpenAttention spends budget on exact rows and leaves the rest in normalization as log-count mean proxies. TTR maps whole groups to regression coefficients with no per-item invertibility guarantee. Trace where missing information goes rather than counting output vectors. Local formulas or short runs do not rank long-text capability.

fields.title: October 29: new methods and evidence boundaries
fields.body: Select-TTT changes how strongly each context chunk writes to fast weights based on current query token probability mass; apply-before-write preserves temporal order. Clipping can leave the total below the chunk count and must not be renormalized to fake conservation. Sleep separates active learning from offline consolidation; locally only LTI reward runs. Its full method trains added parameters, so the reward operator does not establish memory written into the model.

fields.title: Write state first, then choose which segments to read
fields.body: Mamba's selective recurrence controls what enters a state; MERLIN assumes compressed segments and readouts already exist and routes the current query among them. Equal key means can hide a few strong matches. Raw second moments recover aligned variance but not missing within-segment detail. Eq. 9 normalizes means and variances separately before mixing, unlike mixing logits then softmax. Equal-length segments and causal visibility are required.

fields.question: Why are changing RoPE and switching to recurrence not the same fix for a forgotten early one-off identifier?
fields.answer: RoPE changes position in QK, not access to original evidence. Mamba changes selective state writing; if it omits the identifier, no original KV remains to query. Diagnose position distortion, invisibility, or compression loss first, then decide whether to use detail access such as NSA.
fields.example: An order ID appears once on the contract cover. Correct relative positions do not ensure it is read, and bounded state does not retain every ID.

fields.question: How do selected NSA blocks and OpenAttention unread-cluster proxies handle omissions differently?
fields.answer: NSA gates overview, selected blocks, and recent-window outputs; OpenAttention includes unread clusters as count-corrected proxies in the same attention normalization as exact rows. Multiple coverage paths and tail mass/value approximation can both lose within-group details.
fields.example: One outlier among 100 records can be diluted by either a coarse summary or a mean; test whether selection routes it to an exact read.

fields.question: Do TTR input-wise fitting and Mamba per-token state updates mean the deployment model trains its weights?
fields.answer: No. TTR solves coefficients in the current group's forward pass using outer-trained targets and regularization. Mamba uses fixed parameters and current tokens to update state. These are input-dependent computation or runtime state, not optimizer updates, and have different solve versus recurrence costs.
fields.example: One frozen model can produce different states and coefficients for two texts without writing a new checkpoint.

fields.question: What actual execution is evidenced by query-conditioned write coefficients versus Sleep reward changes?
fields.answer: Local Select-TTT updates a small fast-weight matrix, allowing pre-write outputs and final state checks. Local Sleep returns a reward without an optimizer or parameter expansion. Neither establishes long-context capability, and reward is not long-term retention.
fields.example: Updating a memory table and scoring a continuation 0.9 are different evidence.

fields.question: Does adding a second moment turn MERLIN's bounded Mamba-like state into full attention?
fields.answer: No. The moment estimates alignment variance between the query and each segment's routing keys to combine readouts. Token values remain compressed and are not individually normalized; an added access cue cannot reverse compression.
fields.example: Means of 1 do not distinguish a segment of all ones from a segment of −1 and 3. Variance distinguishes them but cannot reconstruct every original record.

fields.summary: Initial version: compared position, selective state, three sparse read paths, tail proxies, and forward regression compression by how they preserve and recover history.

Select-TTT scales fast-weight writes by query token probability mass and preserves apply-before-write order. Do not renormalize the clipped total to the chunk count. Sleep uses distinct active and consolidation stages; only its LTI reward runs here. Unlike frozen-parameter state updates, full Sleep trains extensions, which a reward operator cannot establish.

Reviewed MERLIN Eqs. 7–9: distinguish raw second moments, alignment variance, and two-softmax gated readout from Mamba recurrence; document completed causal segments, the external current segment, and the lack of exact attention.
